summary: Close P0 runtime gaps with a policy-pinned built-in provider composition boundary, six qualified connector reconciliation bridges, executable drift actions, atomic Inbox/webhook consumption, non-secret runtime configuration and a green frontend gate.

impacts.evidence: Runtime configuration and all bridge data reads use organization/workspace scope under forced RLS.
Provider configuration is explicitly non-secret; credentials remain callback-scoped through SecretProvider and audit summaries exclude payloads.
Additive runtime-config GET/PUT operations were added and all public SDKs regenerated; existing operations are unchanged.

Kafka events now enter inboxrepo-owned transactions; webhook delivery rows and the immutable inbox receipt commit atomically before the Kafka offset is acknowledged. Event schemas and topics are unchanged.

Connector SDK v1 remains unchanged. A single policy-pinned built-in composition module may link only active registered provider implementations; App/Core and ordinary Platform packages remain provider-neutral.
Expand migration 000068 adds forced-RLS, versioned non-secret connector runtime configuration.

Only the exact policy-declared built-in composition module may import active registered providers. Provider packages retain SDK-only authority; host egress is HTTPS-only, DNS-pinned and redirect-disabled, and runtime config rejects secret-bearing keys recursively.
ActionExecutor is fail-closed: only provably safe mapping/inbound repairs and supported WooCommerce product writes auto-fix; unsupported outbound writes notify rather than claim success.
Runtime-config writes are audited without payloads; reconciliation mutations use deterministic idempotency-derived evidence IDs.
Mapping repair, catalog repair, WooCommerce writes, notifications and approval requests use stable action idempotency keys and replay-safe persistence.
Kafka-to-webhook projection uses the inbox-owned PostgreSQL transaction, so delivery enqueue plus inbox receipt are atomic and the Kafka offset is committed only after that transaction succeeds.
Source-unavailable conditions retain bounded machine error codes; runtime config has explicit version/conflict behavior.
Migration 000068 is expand-only; old binaries ignore the table and connector writes remain capability-gated.

Architecture regression tests prove the composition module accepts registered providers and rejects unregistered imports; frontend, SDK, migration/catalog and targeted runtime tests cover the remaining P0 closure.
